sections.h2: South Salt Lake at a glance
sections.html:
South Salt Lake is a compact city of about 6.9 square miles sitting directly south of Salt Lake City, with the Jordan River to the west, 500 East and 700 East to the east, 2100 South to the north and 3900 South to the south. The 2020 Census counted 26,777 people in 10,448 households, which works out to roughly 3,857 people per square mile.

Only 38.2% of homes are owner-occupied, so many of the people selling here are landlords. Median value for owner-occupied homes runs about $410,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $1,451. The value is a survey median, so your house may land above or below it depending on condition, lot and location.

The city is its own municipality. Building permits, code enforcement and business licenses go through South Salt Lake City Hall at 220 East Morris Avenue.

Location is the big selling point. The Spaghetti Bowl, where I-15, I-80 and SR-201 meet, is at the northwest corner, and I-15 and I-80 each have local interchanges.

  • TRAX light rail runs along roughly 200 West with three stations in the city. Blue, Red and Green lines meet at Central Pointe station.
  • The S Line streetcar opened in December 2013 and stops at Central Pointe, South Main, 300 East and 500 East.
  • The average commute is about 20 minutes.

Measure how far your address is from a stop before you list it. Walking distance is one of the first things buyers ask.
Granite School District covers the city. Boundaries follow Granite School District maps, so check the specific address if a buyer asks which school a child would attend.

The city enforces yard, vehicle and property maintenance rules and usually opens with a courtesy notice. Over 90% of issues are settled through communication and education, but unresolved cases can lead to fines and civil prosecution.

TopicRequirement
Lawns and ground coverUnder 6 inches; control noxious weeds
Vehicle parkingPaved surfaces only, not grass, dirt or gravel
Inoperable or unregistered vehiclesA public nuisance after 30 consecutive days
Trash binsOut by 7:00 a.m. on collection day, back in afterward
Sidewalk snowClear within 24 hours, leaving a path at least 42 inches wide

If you inherited a neglected house, an open violation can be attached to the property. Clear it before you sell and a buyer has one fewer thing to ask about. Call 801-464-6757 to check a property.

Landlords need a city license, and inspections come first. On-site inspections by the Building Department and Fire Marshal are required before a license is granted, and operating without an approved license is a Class C misdemeanor. Landlords who finish the Good Landlord Program, with training every three years, written leases and background checks on adult occupants, get a significant reduction in license fees. Business licenses are not transferable, so someone who buys a rental has to apply on their own.

For short-term stays, a pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026 stays in place for 180 days or until a new code is adopted. It defines a short-term rental as a stay under 30 consecutive days, requires an owner-occupied duplex, owner-occupied rental or a property owned by a primary resident, and bars short-term rentals in accessory dwelling units.

The county sends out the bill, and November 30 is the payment deadline. Come December 1, anything unpaid for the current year is delinquent and picks up a charge of 2.5% or $10 per parcel, whichever is larger. Settle everything by January 31 and that charge is cut to 1%.

Notices of value go out by July 22. To contest yours, reach the Board of Equalization by September 15 or within 45 days of the notice, whichever date falls later. Owners living in the home get a 45% exemption, leaving 55% of market value taxable. Landlords and second-home owners get no such break, a point worth remembering if the house you are selling is an investment.

Visit the Treasurer at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200. The Recorder, who files the deed, works from Suite N1-600 in that same building.

sections.h2: Selling a house with tenants or a lapsed license
sections.html:
No bank underwriting means a cash buyer is not held up by deferred repairs or sitting tenants. You give us the address, the condition and what you want out of the sale, and we put a written offer in front of you. A title or escrow company runs the closing and has the deed recorded with the county.

If the property is a rental, settle the lease, security deposits and city license steps with the buyer before the closing date. Bring the leases, the deposit records and the current license, if there is one, to the signing.

An unpaid tax bill does not stop a sale, but it does need to be cleared. Ask the title company to pull the current balance from the Treasurer, and expect the amount to be taken from your proceeds at closing. If you are mid-year, the current year is split between you and the buyer by the days each of you owns the house. Landlords should also check whether any city license fee is outstanding, since the buyer starts with their own license anyway.

sections.h2: How the closing goes, step by step
sections.html:
First, request an offer and compare it with what a listing would net after commissions, repairs and carrying costs. Second, pick a closing date that fits your move. Third, the title company opens the file, orders a payoff on any mortgage and checks for liens or open violations. Fourth, you sign at the title office, and the funds are sent to you once the deed is recorded. If tenants live in the house, bring the lease and tell them about the sale in writing as the lease requires.

Skipped on a cash sale: staging, open houses, buyer repair requests and waiting on a lender appraisal. That is a real saving of time for someone managing a rental or an inherited house.

A listing suits a house in good shape that you can show and wait on. Cash suits the house with tenants, deferred repairs, a lapsed license or a clock ticking. Ask for an offer, run the numbers against a likely listing price, and walk away if it does not work. There is no cost to asking.

sections.h2: What to check before accepting an offer
sections.html:
• Whether every unit in a duplex or converted basement has a building permit on file.
  • Whether the rental license is current and inspections were passed.
  • Any open code complaint about weeds, vehicles or trash.
  • Who lives in the house, and whether a lease or deposit must transfer.

A cash buyer who hears these answers early can offer a cleaner number.

faqs.q: Which county is South Salt Lake in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The county Assessor values your house, the Treasurer collects the tax and the Recorder files your deed. Granite School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When is South Salt Lake property tax due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the late fee falls to 1% if you pay by January 31.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my South Salt Lake house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a rental license with on-site building and fire inspections first, and operating without one is a Class C misdemeanor. Good Landlord certification reduces the fee.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: Only under the city's pending ordinance, which limits short-term rentals to owner-occupied or primary-resident properties and bars them in accessory dwelling units. It was issued October 15, 2026, so check the city's page for the final code.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: Median value of owner-occupied homes is $410,200 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, so your house may differ based on condition, lot and location.
